review_type: Direct model visual inspection of actual completed frames and native-resolution crops. Not a human panel, calibrated perceptual benchmark, or a numerical photorealism certificate.
comparison: The original wide camera is retained. A separately executed 1200x800 comparison restores V10 sun direction, exposure, white balance, sample budgets and opaque filter blend. It keeps V11 geometry, materials and atmosphere implementation, and is not a geometry-only ablation.
visible_changes: The previously broad smooth mountains now have more irregular silhouettes, ridges, spurs and incision.
The large right-hand rocks are visibly fractured and surface-damaged rather than the V10 rounded, camouflage-colored forms.
Near-shore vegetation is larger and more numerous, with stems and attached leaves rather than mostly distant sparse plants.
The foreground has more resolved relief and fragments; the final image is natively 1920x1280 rather than V10 1200x800.
remaining_failures: The wide frame still reads as a procedurally constructed environment rather than a photograph. Increased detail and changed silhouettes do not establish the requested photographic jump.

The opaque foreground and shoreline still resemble one lumpy or clay-like substrate. Native-resolution crops expose smooth rounded relief and insufficient material-specific surface structure between stones.
Hero-rock surfaces are still overly uniform in hue and generic pitting. More geometric damage does not provide convincing distinct geology.
The mountains retain repetitive local relief and nearly uniform brown material treatment. They lack convincing differentiation between exposed formations, talus and alluvial deposits.
The plants remain recognizably procedural and their twig/leaf patterns repeat across the scene.
The pool has an overly designed-looking basin/shelf transition and broad repeated-looking illumination patterns. No all-root reference caustics validation was performed.

The independent shoreline view does not solve the problem: it magnifies the clay-like ground and generic fractured fragments. It is retained as a diagnostic view, not presented as a more photorealistic substitute for the wide landscape.
unfiltered_outputs: Saved native RGB and sixteen-band radiance, with contribution clamping disabled. The unfiltered PNG still uses the declared display exposure, white balance and tone transform.
postprocessing: Two geometry-guided non-neural radiance-filter passes, with additional sky-only filtering. The specified sediment/crust blend retains half of the unfiltered residual. No generative enhancement, extra grain, photographic backplate or upscaling.
rejected_test: A different sun direction with procedural cloud lighting was actually rendered as light_study and rejected because its visible cloud shapes and reflection stripe were less natural. It is not included among finished deliverables.
